back: A translator that converts the whole of a high-level program to object code before it is run.
A translator that analyses and executes a program one statement at a time without producing a complete translated copy.
A translator for assembly language, producing machine code.
Source code is the program as written; object code is the machine code produced by translating it.
Compiled: runs faster, source hidden, errors reported after translation. Interpreted: quick to test, errors at the statement, source needed.
Source is compiled to byte code, which a virtual machine interprets; portable across computers.
Prompts, dynamic syntax checking, pretty-print, collapsing blocks, single stepping, breakpoints, variable and expression report windows.
A breakpoint pauses at a chosen line; single stepping runs one statement at a time; the report window shows the variables.
Interpreter while developing and testing; compiler for the finished program that is run many times.
